issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Milkable', but the solution implementation defines an interface named 'Dairy' (and leaves Milkable.java empty). Several animal classes in the solution implement 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable', and the template Main references 'Milkable'. This name/type mismatch prevents students from aligning their implementations with the provided solution or template (compilation errors or confusion which interface to implement).
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent interface name across all artifacts. Either: (a) rename the solution's Dairy interface to Milkable (and have Seal and Goat implement Milkable), and remove or populate Milkable.java appropriately; or (b) update the problem statement and template to refer to Dairy instead of Milkable. Ensure Milkable/Dairy.java declares messageOnMilk() with the signature specified in the problem.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Milkable' (with method messageOnMilk()), but the solution implementation introduces an interface named 'Dairy' that provides messageOnMilk() and has the domain classes implement 'Dairy'. Additionally, a Milkable.java file in the solution is empty. This inconsistent naming (Milkable vs Dairy) refers to the same conceptual entity (the milkable capability) using different identifiers across artifacts and will confuse students trying to map the requirements (which mention Milkable) to the provided/expected implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (file Dairy.java -> Milkable.java) and have Goat and Seal implement Milkable, or alternatively populate Milkable.java in the solution with the intended interface and have classes implement it. This restores a single consistent identifier 'Milkable' as used in the problem and template.
